claims.title: Landing-bucket extracts may be readable on the scheduler read path
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`, an attacker with a position on the landing-network path can intercept the partner extract files as `process:ingest-scheduler` lists and reads them. The files contain health-related claim records with names and dates of birth; captured records can subsequently be correlated with the normalized records loaded into `store:claims-warehouse`. This is conditional on the currently unverified transport setting, not an assertion that the object-storage API is plaintext.

quotes.text: The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the flow remains within `boundary:landing-network` and an attacker needs a network-path foothold, conditional on its unknown transport encryption; impact is high because the intercepted extracts contain member names, dates of birth, and health-related claim data.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted object-storage transport
mitigations.detail: Set and document TLS-protected `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`, including certificate validation for the storage endpoint.
Segment scheduler-to-storage traffic and restrict diagnostic packet capture and network observation privileges.

claims.title: Airflow connection strings and partner keys may be exposed in transit
claims.description: If transport protection is absent on `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`, an on-path attacker can intercept the connection strings and partner SFTP keys that `process:ingest-scheduler` retrieves from `store:airflow-metadata-database`. A recovered partner key enables subsequent access attempts against the partner upload path and can expose future claims extracts. This is conditional on the flow's unknown protocol, authentication, and encryption state.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because interception requires a foothold on the internal landing-network path and is conditional on three unverified flow controls; impact is high because `store:airflow-metadata-database` holds credentials and secrets, including partner keys that can enable later access.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate metadata-database connections
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server validation and workload authentication for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`.
Move partner credentials to a dedicated secret manager, issue short-lived or regularly rotated credentials, and rotate the existing onboarding keys.

claims.title: Cross-zone transform requests may disclose pipeline metadata
claims.description: `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>process:spark-transform-job>trigger-transform` crosses from `boundary:landing-network` to `boundary:warehouse-network`, yet its transport encryption is unknown. If that control is absent, an on-path observer can intercept run requests naming the file being processed, revealing the timing and identity of incoming claims extracts. That metadata can guide targeted collection against the corresponding landing-bucket files and warehouse load cycle; it is not a claim that the trigger request itself carries claim rows.

quotes.text: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the request crosses the landing-to-warehouse boundary and encryption is unverified, though an attacker still needs path access; impact is low because the stated request names a file rather than carrying claim records.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS or mTLS for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>process:spark-transform-job>trigger-transform` and verify the receiving Spark endpoint.
Pass non-sensitive job identifiers rather than meaningful file names where the transform service can resolve the work item server-side.

claims.title: Normalized claims may be readable while loaded into the warehouse
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records`, an attacker positioned on that path can intercept normalized claim rows as `process:spark-transform-job` loads them into `store:claims-warehouse`. The capture exposes member-identifying health data and can be correlated with the analyst-query path to target affected members. This is conditional on the unknown transport encryption setting.

quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the Spark-to-warehouse path is internal and requires a network foothold, conditional on unknown encryption; impact is high because the loaded records are normalized claims containing member-identifying health data.

mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce TLS for `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records`, with authenticated service-to-service access.
Tokenize or encrypt the highest-risk member-identifying fields before the load where warehouse processing does not require cleartext values.

claims.title: Analyst warehouse queries may expose member data on the network
claims.description: `entity:data-analyst` queries `store:claims-warehouse` through `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries`, whose `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If transport encryption is absent, an on-path observer in the warehouse network can intercept query results containing member identifiers. Because analysts are granted the whole dataset, the observer can capture broad results rather than only a narrowly scoped report. This is conditional on the unverified transport setting.

quotes.text: Analysts query the warehouse directly. They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because interception requires warehouse-network path access and is conditional on unknown encryption; impact is high because the queries can return the dataset-wide member-identifying health records.

mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce TLS for `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries`, including client validation of the warehouse endpoint.
Split or restrict member-identifying columns so ordinary analyst queries do not return them by default.

claims.title: A landing-bucket copy may expose claims extracts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` is confidential and holds PII and health-related partner extracts, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains its media, operational copy, snapshot, or decommissioned storage can read the extracts without using the SFTP upload or scheduler access paths. The disclosed member names and dates of birth can be correlated with subsequent warehouse records. This is conditional and does not assert that the bucket is unencrypted.

quotes.text: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted
The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on unknown at-rest encryption because a copied storage artifact bypasses application authentication if protection is absent; impact is high because the confidential bucket contains member-identifying health claim extracts.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for bucket data and copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the bucket's at-rest posture and require managed-key encryption for the bucket, snapshots, exports, and backups, with tightly controlled key use.
Limit who can create, copy, restore, or download bucket snapshots and audit those operations.

claims.title: A metadata-database copy may disclose partner credentials and connection strings
claims.description: `store:airflow-metadata-database` holds connection strings and partner SFTP keys, is classified confidential, and has unknown `encryption_at_rest`. If its storage or an operational copy is unencrypted, an attacker holding that copy can recover the secrets without authenticating as `process:ingest-scheduler`. The recovered partner keys can be used to access or impersonate the upload path, exposing future partner claim extracts. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption state.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted or whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on unknown at-rest encryption because an unprotected storage copy can be read outside the live application path; impact is high because the confidential store contains credentials and secrets that enable further access.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the metadata database and every operational copy
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce managed-key encryption at rest for `store:airflow-metadata-database`, including backups, snapshots, and restores.
Move SFTP keys and connection secrets into a dedicated secret manager, rotate the unchanged onboarding keys, and minimize secret retrieval privileges.

claims.title: A claims-warehouse copy may disclose the normalized member dataset
claims.description: `store:claims-warehouse` is confidential, contains PII and health data, and has unknown `encryption_at_rest`. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a warehouse export, backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can read normalized claims directly rather than going through the SSO-protected analyst query path. A raw copy can expose the full member dataset at once. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest control.

quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the warehouse's unknown at-rest encryption because a storage-layer copy bypasses SSO if encryption is absent; impact is high because the confidential warehouse holds normalized PII and health claim records.

mitigations.summary: Verify warehouse encryption and protect copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest encryption configuration for `store:claims-warehouse` and require encryption and access controls for exports, backups, snapshots, and replicas.
Separate export permissions from normal query permissions and log or alert on bulk extraction operations.

claims.title: Code running in the scheduler can read every landing-bucket extract
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` lists `store:landing-bucket` nightly and reads every file present through `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`; the flow's authentication is unknown. An attacker who gains code execution in the scheduler can use that existing reader path to read all partner extracts, including claims with member names and dates of birth. The disclosure can then be matched to the transform runs the scheduler initiates and the corresponding warehouse loads. This finding is conditional on compromise of the scheduler and identifies the unverified reader authentication as information that must be resolved.

quotes.text: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.
The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because an attacker must first execute code in `process:ingest-scheduler`, but its storage-reader authentication is unstated; impact is high because that reader obtains all partner extracts containing member-identifying health data.

mitigations.summary: Use a narrowly scoped scheduler identity
mitigations.detail: Require a workload identity for the scheduler and limit it to the specific partner prefixes and object operations required for each run.
Audit scheduler object reads and alert when its access pattern differs from the nightly expected files.

claims.title: Code running in the scheduler can recover metadata-database secrets
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` reads the connection strings and partner keys in `store:airflow-metadata-database` through `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`, whose authentication is unknown. An attacker running code in the scheduler can recover those secrets through the same legitimate read path, then use partner keys to seek access to the landing upload path and future claims extracts. This is conditional on scheduler compromise; encryption at rest would not prevent an authorized live reader from receiving the secrets.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker needs execution in `process:ingest-scheduler`, while authentication on its secret-read flow is unknown; impact is high because recovered partner keys and connection strings can enable subsequent access to sensitive extracts.

mitigations.summary: Give the scheduler only just-in-time secret access
mitigations.detail: Use a secret manager with short-lived, workload-bound credentials and grant `process:ingest-scheduler` access only to the secrets required for its active run.
Replace the unchanged onboarding keys with per-partner rotated credentials and revoke keys that have been stored in Airflow metadata.

claims.title: Dataset-wide analyst access discloses member-identifying claim data
claims.description: An authorized `entity:data-analyst` can use `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` to query `store:claims-warehouse` under a dataset-wide grant that includes member-identifying columns. A curious, malicious, or compromised analyst account can therefore read claim records beyond a task that does not require identifying information. The resulting identifiers and health-related claims can be exported or correlated across the warehouse dataset; the issue is the grant's breadth, not an SSO authentication failure.

quotes.text: They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because an analyst already has SSO-authenticated direct query access and needs only to misuse or lose that account; impact is high because the stated dataset-wide grant includes member-identifying columns in a confidential warehouse holding PII and health data.

mitigations.summary: Restrict analyst access to minimum necessary fields
mitigations.detail: Separate member-identifying columns into protected views or datasets and grant analysts only the fields and rows required for their assigned analysis.
Require approval for re-identification access, log queries against identifying columns, and alert on bulk or enumeration-shaped result sets.
